newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Oil price to lift BP Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Oil price to lift BP Q1 profit.

text.p: Higher oil prices are set to fuel British Petroleum Co Plc's first-quarter profit which is due to be released on Tuesday.
Analysts predict replacement cost net profit before exceptional items between 657-725 million stg, up from 633 million a year ago.
The expected profit rise would come after Royal Dutch/Shell Group reported flat first quarter results on Thursday.
The difference stems from BP's greater emphasis on oil production, which makes it benefit more from a higher crude price than Shell, which is more geared to the downstream business, analysts said.
But like Shell, BP will have felt the impact of relatively mild European winter weather, resulting in lower gas sales and holding back a profit rise in the exploration and production sector.
Downstream refining and marketing results are expected to be slightly higher amid margin improvement in Europe.
The first positive effects of the European downstream joint venture with Mobil Corp may also become visible, broker Lehman Brothers wrote in a note today.
Lehman believes BP's chemicals operations will have benefitted from strong demand, but suffered from the weak mark against the pound.
Irene Himona, analyst at SocGen, also pointed at higher feedstock prices and expects chemical profits to fall to 107 million stg from 128 million.
Higher taxes will also put a break on BP's profit growth, analysts said.
